authority,licensing,responsibility	Driver Licensing Authority
Person
The Driver Licensing Authority holds ultimate responsibility for issuing, renewing, suspending, or cancelling a person's driver licence.

information,licensing,medical criteria	Driver Licensing Authority
Health Professional
The Driver Licensing Authority receives details of medical criteria not met and evidence of criteria met from the Health Professional to inform licensing decisions.

conditional licence,conditions,licensing	Driver Licence
Health Professional
The Health Professional provides proposed conditions and monitoring requirements for a conditional licence to be issued.

fitness to drive,medical assessment	Health Professional
Person
A person's fitness to drive is assessed by a Health Professional who evaluates medical criteria and potential impairments.

health assessment,medical condition	Hearing Impairment
Medical Criteria
Hearing impairment is considered as a specific medical criterion that may affect fitness to drive.

health assessment,medical condition	Medical Criteria
Visual Impairment
Visual impairment is considered as a specific medical criterion that may affect fitness to drive.

health assessment,medical condition	Cognitive Impairment
Medical Criteria
Cognitive impairment is considered as a specific medical criterion that may affect fitness to drive.

combined effect,concurrent conditions	Hearing Impairment
Multiple Medical Conditions
Hearing impairment may combine with other medical conditions to affect overall fitness to drive.

combined effect,concurrent conditions	Multiple Medical Conditions
Visual Impairment
Visual impairment may combine with other medical conditions to affect overall fitness to drive.

combined effect,concurrent conditions	Cognitive Impairment
Multiple Medical Conditions
Cognitive impairment may combine with other medical conditions to affect overall fitness to drive.

accreditation,professional certification	Audiologist
Audiology Australia
An audiologist is accredited by Audiology Australia.

accreditation,professional certification	Audiologist
Australian College of Audiology
An audiologist is accredited by the Australian College of Audiology.

accreditation,professional certification	Audiometrist
Australian College of Audiology
An audiometrist is accredited by the Australian College of Audiology.

data.tgt_id: Hearing Aid Audiology Society of Australia
data.content:
accreditation,professional certification	Audiometrist
Hearing Aid Audiology Society of Australia
An audiometrist is accredited by the Hearing Aid Audiology Society of Australia.

health,impairment,reduction	Comorbidities
Functional Abilities
Comorbidities may lead to a general reduction in functional abilities.

impairment,performance,safety	Driving
Functional Abilities
Reduced functional abilities may impair the ability to drive safely.

mobility,physical limitation,reduction	Musculoskeletal Changes
Neck Rotation
Musculoskeletal changes can result in reduced neck rotation.

impairment,requirement,safety	Driving
Neck Rotation
Reduced neck rotation may impair driving performance due to its necessity for vehicle operation.

cognitive impact,response,slowing	Comorbidities
Reaction Times
Comorbidities may cause slower reaction times.

impairment,requirement,safety	Driving
Reaction Times
Slower reaction times may impair driving performance due to the need for quick responses.

awareness,maintenance,state	Alertness
Vigilance
Vigilance is maintained through alertness.

maintenance,readiness,state	Alertness
Arousal
Alertness is maintained through arousal.

assessment,clinical evaluation,threshold	Commercial standards
Hearing loss
The standard requires an initial clinical assessment to detect hearing loss; if the loss is present, the person must be referred for audiometry.

eligibility,fitness,restriction	Commercial standards
Unconditional licence
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence if they have unaided hearing loss of 40 dB or greater in the better ear.

issuance,periodic evaluation,review	Conditional licence
Driver licensing authority
The driver licensing authority may consider issuing a conditional licence subject to periodic review based on various factors.

assessment criteria,compliance	Commercial standards
Driver licensing authority
The driver licensing authority evaluates whether the commercial standards can be met by a driver with hearing impairment.

accommodation,distraction,noise amplification	Commercial standards
Hearing aid
The standard may be met using a hearing aid, though noise amplification can cause driver distraction requiring individualized assessment.

assessment information,medical input	Conditional licence
ENT specialist
An ENT specialist provides information to the driver licensing authority regarding whether the commercial standard can be met.

assessment information,medical input	Audiologist
Conditional licence
An audiologist provides information to the driver licensing authority regarding whether the commercial standard can be met.

evaluation,fitness determination,requirement	Conditional licence
Practical driver assessment
The results of a practical driver assessment may be taken into account when considering a conditional licence if required.

driving capability,impairment	Fitness to drive
Hearing loss and deafness
Hearing loss and deafness impact the fitness to drive by reducing auditory input necessary for scanning the driving environment.

coexistence,impairment	Hearing loss and deafness
Vision and eye disorders
Hearing loss and deafness may coexist with vision and eye disorders, potentially compromising adaptive driving capabilities.

coexistence,impairment	Hearing loss and deafness
Musculoskeletal conditions
Hearing loss and deafness may coexist with musculoskeletal conditions, which can compromise physical mobility needed for driving.

coexistence,impairment	Hearing loss and deafness
Visual impairment
Hearing loss and deafness may coexist with visual impairment, affecting the ability to scan the driving environment.

coexistence,impairment	Hearing loss and deafness
Mobility impairment
Hearing loss and deafness may coexist with mobility impairment, reducing physical capacity to operate a vehicle.

coexistence,impairment	Cognitive impairment
Hearing loss and deafness
Hearing loss and deafness may coexist with cognitive impairment, particularly in older people, affecting overall adaptive capabilities.

assessment,guidance	Hearing loss and deafness
Part A 2.2.8. Multiple medical conditions
Part A 2.2.8. Multiple medical conditions provides guidance for assessing individuals with multiple medical conditions, including those with hearing loss.

driving performance,risk assessment,safety	Hearing Loss
Motor Vehicle Crash Risk
Analysis of quality studies indicates that hearing loss does not increase the risk of motor vehicle crashes.

compensation,driving adaptation,sensory substitution	Hearing Loss
Visual Cues
Individuals with hearing loss often compensate for their disability by relying more heavily on visual information while driving.

sensory compensation,tactile feedback,vehicle awareness	Hearing Loss
Vibrations
Drivers with hearing loss may utilize vibrations felt through the vehicle to detect mechanical states or environmental events.

auditory perception,safety warning,traffic environment	Functional Hearing
Railway Crossings
Functional hearing enables drivers to sense auditory cues associated with railway crossings, such as approaching train warnings.

auditory alert,emergency awareness,traffic environment	First Responder Sirens
Functional Hearing
Functional hearing allows drivers to detect sirens from first responders, which serve as critical auditory cues in the driving environment.

instrument monitoring,safety alerts,vehicle status	Functional Hearing
Vehicle Technology Systems
Functional hearing is utilized to sense auditory notifications from vehicle technology systems regarding alarms and warning states.

consideration,granting,information,issuance,medical condition,regulation,review	Conditional Licence
Driver Licensing Authority
The driver licensing authority grants conditional licences while taking into account the nature of the driving task and the medical condition.<SEP>The driver licensing authority may consider granting a conditional licence based on the information received from assessments.<SEP>The authority is responsible for considering and issuing conditional licenses subject to periodic review.<SEP>The authority considers issuing a conditional licence subject to periodic review based on specific criteria.

commercial vehicle,heavy vehicle,licence status	Conditional Licence
Farmer
A farmer requiring a commercial vehicle licence for occasional use of a heavy vehicle has a specific licence status distinct from other drivers.

driving task,licence status	Conditional Licence
Interstate Multiple Combination Vehicle Driver
An interstate multiple combination vehicle driver has a different licence status compared to a farmer due to the nature of their driving task.

advice,examination,medical condition	Driver Licensing Authority
Examining Health Professional
The examining health professional provides advice to the driver licensing authority when examining a person regarding their medical condition.

driving effects,legal obligation,notification	Driver Licensing Authority
Patient
Patients have a legal obligation to notify the driver licensing authority where their condition is likely to affect driving.

assessment,driving,eligibility,fitness,standard	Conditional Licence
Hearing Aid
The inability to meet standard driving requirements with a hearing aid does not disqualify a person from obtaining a conditional licence.<SEP>The standard for a conditional license is evaluated to determine if it can be met with the use of a hearing aid.

assessment,assessment input,eligibility,information,medical opinion,specialist	Conditional Licence
ENT Specialist
An ENT specialist may conduct an individualized assessment to determine a person's eligibility for a conditional licence.<SEP>An ENT specialist provides information regarding the nature of driving tasks and hearing conditions relevant to the license.<SEP>Information provided by an ENT specialist is taken into account when considering a conditional licence.

assessment,assessment input,eligibility,information,medical opinion,specialist	Audiologist
Conditional Licence
An audiologist may conduct an individualized assessment to determine a person's eligibility for a conditional licence.<SEP>An audiologist provides information regarding hearing status relevant to the conditional license assessment.<SEP>Information provided by an audiologist is taken into account when considering a conditional licence.

adaptation,childhood deafness,eligibility	Conditional Licence
Medical History
A person's medical history, such as childhood deafness leading to good adaptation, is considered when determining eligibility for a conditional licence.

driving behavior,eligibility,history	Conditional Licence
Driving Record
The person's driving record before and since the hearing loss is assessed to determine their eligibility for a conditional licence.

assessment,distances,roads,vehicle type	Conditional Licence
Driving Task
The nature of the driving task, including vehicle type and road conditions, is considered in the assessment for a conditional licence.

assessment,assistive devices,ergonomics	Conditional Licence
Driving Cab
The ergonomics of the driving cab and available assistive devices are factors considered in the assessment for a conditional licence.

assessment,concomitant condition,medical	Conditional Licence
Vision Impairment
Concomitant medical conditions such as vision impairment are considered alongside hearing loss when assessing eligibility for a conditional licence.

assessment,concomitant condition,medical	Cognitive Impairment
Conditional Licence
Concomitant medical conditions such as cognitive impairment are considered alongside hearing loss when assessing eligibility for a conditional licence.

assistive technologies,evaluation,report,required,requirement	Conditional Licence
Practical Driver Assessment
A practical driver assessment may be required, and the resulting report can advise on assistive technologies as a licence condition.<SEP>A practical driver assessment may be required as part of the conditional license process if further individualized assessment is needed.

condition,natural history,review frequency	Conditional Licence
Health Professional
A health professional advises on the frequency of periodic reviews determined by the natural history of the person's condition.

distraction,fitness to drive,hearing aid	Conditional Licence
Noise Amplification
Noise amplification from wearing a hearing aid may lead to driver distraction, warranting an assessment to determine fitness to drive without the aid.

Compensation,Responsiveness,Safety	Commercial Vehicle Drivers
Hearing Loss
Drivers of commercial vehicles require the capacity to respond to critical events despite potential hearing loss, as driving ability itself may not be affected.

Auditory Response,Environmental Monitoring,Safety	Commercial Vehicle Drivers
Sirens
Drivers must respond to sirens as part of their capacity to monitor environmental situations involving emergency signals.

Auditory Response,Environmental Monitoring,Safety	Commercial Vehicle Drivers
Rail Crossings
Drivers must respond to rail crossings as part of their capacity to monitor environmental situations involving emergency signals.

Auditory Response,Environmental Monitoring,Safety	Commercial Vehicle Drivers
Emergency Signals
Drivers must respond to emergency signals as part of their capacity to monitor environmental situations involving critical events.

Compensation,Limitations,Safety	Commercial Vehicle Drivers
Vision
Relying solely on vision to compensate for significant hearing loss in a commercial vehicle is challenging due to the need for auditory input.

Attention,Visual Demands,Workload	Commercial Vehicle Cabin
Commercial Vehicle Drivers
The internal cabin places additional attentional, workload, and visual demands on drivers for tasks such as checking displays and using communication systems.

Information Exchange,Task Execution,Workload	Commercial Vehicle Cabin
Communication Systems
Drivers use communication systems within the cabin to undertake tasks that contribute to increased workload and visual demands.

Information Exchange,Task Execution,Workload	Commercial Vehicle Drivers
Communication Systems
Drivers utilize communication systems to undertake tasks that reduce their capacity to compensate for hearing loss by relying on vision.

adherence,requirement	Compliance
Standard
The concept of compliance involves following the standard.

evaluation,procedure	Clinical Assessment
Standard
Compliance with the standard requires an initial clinical assessment.

detection,indication	Clinical Assessment
Hearing Loss
The clinical assessment is used to identify if hearing loss is possible.

evaluation,subject	Clinical Assessment
Person
A person undergoes the initial clinical assessment.

referral,testing	Audiometry
Hearing Loss
If hearing loss is indicated by the clinical assessment, the person should be referred for audiometry.

eligibility,health criteria,hearing loss	Person
Unconditional Licence
A person is deemed unfit to hold an unconditional licence if they meet specific hearing loss thresholds.

measurement,severity,threshold	Hearing Loss
Person
The condition of having unaided hearing loss greater than or equal to 40 dB in the better ear disqualifies a person from holding the licence.

assessment,auditory range,averaging	Frequencies 0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz
Hearing Loss
The severity of hearing loss is determined by averaging the hearing thresholds across these four specific frequencies.

evaluation,oversight	Driver Licensing Authority
Periodic Review
The authority conducts periodic reviews of conditional licenses, though stable conditions may exempt this requirement.

distraction,side effect	Hearing Aid
Noise Amplification
Wearing a hearing aid may result in noise amplification, which can lead to driver distraction.

evaluation,safety	Noise Amplification
Practical Driver Assessment
If noise amplification causes distraction, an individualized assessment may be warranted to determine fitness to drive without the aid.<SEP>If noise amplification warrants individualised assessment, a practical driver assessment may be required to determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid.

procedure,reference	General Assessment and Management Guidelines
Section 4.2
Section 4.2 contains general assessment and management guidelines referenced for both ENT specialists and audiologists regarding hearing aid usage.
